title: Who is the Holy Trinity?
text: We believe in one God who is three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is called the Holy Trinity. The three Persons are not three different gods. They are one God, equal and always together, and they love each other perfectly. We cannot fully understand this with our minds, because God is much bigger than we are. But we know it because Jesus taught us. When we make the sign of the cross we say, In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, one God. We are baptized in the name of the Trinity, and we end our prayers with glory to the Trinity.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost

title: How can God be three and one?
text: This is a big question, and even grown ups cannot fully explain it. God is a mystery, which means He is so great that our minds cannot hold all of Him. The Church teaches that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three Persons who share one nature, so they are one God. The Father is the source, the Son is born of the Father before all time, and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father. Some people use pictures to help, like the sun with its light and its heat, but every picture is small compared to God. The best thing we can do is pray, thank God, and ask Abouna when we wonder.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is Jesus?
text: Jesus is the Son of God. He is God and He is also truly a human being. Long ago, God the Son came down from heaven to be born of the Virgin Mary so that He could save us. He grew up, taught people, healed the sick and loved everyone. Then He died on the cross for us and rose again on the third day. Now He is alive and always with us. Jesus is our Savior and our friend. When we pray, we are talking to Him. He loves every child very much, and He knows each of us by name.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

title: What is the Incarnation?
text: The Incarnation means that God the Son became a man. The word comes from a word for flesh. Jesus took a real human body and soul from the Virgin Mary by the work of the Holy Spirit, and He stayed fully God at the same time. He did not stop being God when He became human. We celebrate this at the feast of the Nativity. The Church teaches that He is one Christ, perfect God and perfect man, joined together without mixing or change. He became like us so that He could heal us, forgive us and bring us back to God. It is the greatest sign of God's love.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us

title: Who is St. Mary, the Theotokos?
text: St. Mary is the Virgin who gave birth to Jesus. We call her the Theotokos, a Greek word that means the Mother of God, because the baby she carried is God the Son. She said yes to God with a humble heart. She is the most blessed of all women, and the Church honors her more than all the saints. We love her like a spiritual mother and we ask for her prayers. We do not worship her, we worship only God. In church you will see her icon near the front, and we sing her praises often.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we honor St. Mary so much?
text: We honor St. Mary because God chose her to be the mother of Jesus, and she was humble and obedient. When the angel Gabriel told her the news, she answered that she was the handmaid of the Lord. Elizabeth called her blessed among women, and Mary herself said that all generations would call her blessed. Honoring her does not take anything away from Jesus. It is a way of honoring Him, because she is His mother. We ask for her prayers the way we ask a friend or family member to pray for us. The Coptic Church has many hymns and feasts for her, and she is a great example of faith and kindness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is the Holy Spirit?
text: The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity. He is God, equal with the Father and the Son. We believe that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father, and in the Creed we call Him the Lord and Giver of Life. The Holy Spirit comes down on us in baptism and in the sacraments. He helps us to love God, to understand the Bible, to pray and to do what is right. On the day of Pentecost He came upon the apostles like a rushing wind and tongues of fire. The Holy Spirit is our Comforter and helper, and He is always near to us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Baptism
text: Baptism is the first sacrament. In baptism a person is dipped three times in water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. It is like being born again as a child of God. Our sins are washed away and we become members of the Church, the family of God. In the Coptic Church babies are usually baptized, and the priest holds them and dips them in the water. A person is baptized only once in their life. After baptism comes chrismation with the holy oil. Jesus Himself was baptized in the Jordan River, and He told His disciples to baptize all nations.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost

title: Chrismation (Holy Myron)
text: Right after baptism, the priest anoints the newly baptized person with the holy oil called Myron, also called chrism. He makes the sign of the cross with the oil on many parts of the body, like the forehead, hands and feet, and he prays. This is the sacrament of Chrismation, and it is how we receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Myron is very special. It is made and blessed by the Pope together with the bishops, and it is only made once in a long while. We receive Chrismation one time, just like baptism. It seals us as God's own children so the Holy Spirit lives in us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Confession and repentance
text: Confession is the sacrament where we tell our sins to God in front of a priest, and the priest prays the prayer of absolution. This means God forgives us through the Church. We are sorry for what we did wrong, we promise to try again, and we leave with a clean heart. It is not meant to scare us. Confession is like a doctor's visit for the soul, and the priest is a loving father who helps us. We can go to confession many times, and it is a good idea to go regularly, especially before Holy Communion. Ask Abouna when you are ready and how to prepare.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

title: The Eucharist (Holy Communion)
text: The Eucharist is the sacrament where we receive the Body and Blood of Jesus Christ. At the Holy Liturgy, the bread and wine are changed by the Holy Spirit into the true Body and Blood of our Lord. We do not just remember Jesus, we receive Him. Jesus began this at the Last Supper when He gave His disciples bread and wine and told them to do this in remembrance of Him. Communion gives us forgiveness, strength and life with God. The word Eucharist means thanksgiving. We prepare for it by confessing, fasting before it, and coming with a clean heart and respect.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever

title: Matrimony (marriage)
text: Matrimony is the sacrament of marriage. A man and a woman are joined together in front of God and the Church, and the priest prays over them and puts crowns on their heads. The crowns remind us of the joy of the new family and of the crown of the martyrs, which means loving and sacrificing for one another. The couple promise to love each other and to stay together, and God blesses their home. In the Coptic Church, a marriage is a holy path to heaven for both of them, and children are a gift from God. Kids can pray for their parents and family every day.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Priesthood (ordination)
text: Priesthood is the sacrament where a man is set apart to serve God and the Church. The bishop lays his hands on him and prays, and the Holy Spirit gives him the grace to serve. There are three ranks: the deacon, the priest and the bishop. A priest can pray the Holy Liturgy, baptize, hear confessions and bless. He is a shepherd who takes care of God's people, like a father in the family. In the Coptic Church the priest is called Abouna, which means our father. We respect our priests, we pray for them, and we help them in the church. A man is ordained only once for each rank.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Unction of the Sick
text: The sacrament of the Unction of the Sick is for people who are ill. The priests pray over a blessed oil and anoint the sick person with it, asking God to heal their body and soul and forgive their sins. In the Coptic Church the prayer is traditionally done by several priests together, often seven, and it uses readings from the Bible. The Church teaches that God can give healing, comfort or peace, and we trust His love in every case. If someone in your family is sick, you can ask Abouna to visit and pray. Kids can pray for the sick too, and send them a kind card or a call.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Holy Liturgy?
text: The Holy Liturgy is our main worship service. It is the prayer where we gather as God's family to praise Him, hear His Word and receive Holy Communion. We usually have it on Sunday mornings, and on feast days too. Everyone takes part, with the priest, the deacons and the people singing and answering together. It can feel long, but it is the most beautiful time of the week, because heaven and earth are joined together and the angels worship with us. Coming to the Liturgy every Sunday helps us grow close to Jesus and to each other.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Liturgy in simple steps
text: The Holy Liturgy has main parts. First is the offering of the bread and wine, and the prayers of preparation. Then comes the Liturgy of the Word, with readings from the Bible, like the Epistles and the Gospel, and the priest often gives a sermon. After that comes the Liturgy of the Faithful, where we say the Creed and the priest prays over the bread and wine. The Holy Spirit changes them into the Body and Blood of Christ. The service ends with Holy Communion, the thanksgiving and the blessing. There are many hymns, prayers and responses along the way, and everyone takes part.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What do we do during the Liturgy?
text: During the Liturgy we do not just watch, we pray and sing together. We stand when the Gospel is read, because we are listening to Jesus. We say the responses, like Amen and Lord have mercy. We listen quietly to the readings and the sermon. When it is time for Communion, those who are prepared line up with respect and receive it. At the end we receive the blessing and go home in peace. Little ones can follow along by singing, watching the deacons, looking at the icons, and sitting still. If you do not understand something, you can ask Abouna or a servant after church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The church door and the nave
text: When you walk into a Coptic church, you first come to the narthex and the main hall, called the nave. This is where the people stand and pray. The church is a house of God, so we enter with respect, making the sign of the cross and sometimes kissing the cross or the icons. The nave faces east, because Christ is the Sun of Righteousness. The nave represents the earth, where we the people worship God together. The door reminds us that Jesus said He is the door, and we enter into His family through Him. We walk in quietly and keep our voices low.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Haykal?
text: The Haykal is the sanctuary, the most holy part of the church, at the east end behind the iconostasis. It is the place where the altar stands and where the priest and deacons serve the Holy Liturgy. It reminds us of heaven. Only the clergy and those who have blessings to serve there, such as ordained deacons, enter it, and they take off their shoes out of respect, like Moses on holy ground at the burning bush. The word haykal comes from the word for temple. We do not enter the Haykal unless Abouna says it is okay, because it is a very holy place.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the iconostasis?
text: The iconostasis is the wall of icons that stands between the nave and the Haykal. Its name means a stand for icons. On it you will see icons of Jesus, the Virgin Mary, angels, and saints, often with doors in the middle. It does not block us from God. It teaches us that the saints and angels are praying with us, and it shows the holy place beyond. During parts of the Liturgy the curtains or doors are opened, and we see the altar. In many Coptic churches the iconostasis is a beautiful wall with carved wood and paintings. You can look at the icons and say a little prayer to each saint.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The altar
text: The altar is the holy table in the middle of the Haykal. It is the most important place in the church, because this is where the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Jesus during the Holy Liturgy. It is covered with a special cloth, and it holds the cross, the Gospel and the holy vessels. It reminds us of the table of the Last Supper and also of the tomb and the cross where Jesus offered Himself for us. Only the priest and the deacons come near it. Many churches also have more than one altar, but a priest serves the Liturgy on only one altar each day.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Domes and the cross on the church
text: Many Coptic churches have domes on the roof and a cross on top. The dome reminds us of heaven above us, and the church seems to point us up to God. The cross on the top shows that this building belongs to Jesus Christ who died and rose for us, and everyone passing by can see it. Inside the dome there is sometimes an icon of Christ. The church building is shaped to teach us, with the nave for the people, the Haykal for the altar, and the dome and cross pointing to heaven. Whenever you see a cross on a church, you can make the sign of the cross.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we have icons?
text: Icons are holy pictures of Jesus, the Virgin Mary, the angels and the saints. We do not worship them. We worship only God. We kiss them and light candles in front of them to show love and respect, like kissing a photo of someone we love. Icons are also like windows to heaven, helping us remember the saints and their stories, and reminding us that they are alive in Christ and pray for us. They are not just art. Icons are painted with prayer and in a special style, with a gold halo around the heads of the holy ones. Every Coptic home has an icon corner or a few icons.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we use incense?
text: We use incense in church because it is a sign of prayer going up to God. The Bible speaks of prayers rising like incense, and in the Old Testament God asked His people to burn incense in the temple. The priest holds the censer, which is a small metal pot on chains with little bells, and the sweet smoke fills the church. It reminds us of the presence of God and of the sweet smell of prayers. The deacons and the priest cense the altar, the icons, the Gospel and the people. The three chains remind some people of the Trinity. In the Agpeya, some prayers are said with incense too.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we light candles?
text: When we light a candle in church, it is a small prayer. The light reminds us that Jesus is the Light of the world, and that we should shine for Him. The candle burns up while giving light, which teaches us to give ourselves to God and others. People often light a candle in front of an icon, asking God and the saints to pray for a need, or to say thank you. The candle itself does not do the magic, the prayer does. When you light one, make the sign of the cross, say a short prayer, and be careful with the fire. Always ask an adult to help you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The sign of the cross
text: The sign of the cross is a prayer we make with our hand. We touch our forehead, then our chest, then our right shoulder and then our left shoulder, while saying, In the name of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one God. Amen. We remember that Jesus died on the cross for us, and we say we belong to the Holy Trinity. In the Coptic Church we make the sign of the cross with the right hand, going from right to left across the shoulders. We make it when we begin to pray, when we eat, when we pass a church, before a test and when we are afraid. It is a small way to ask for God's help.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Standing, kneeling and prostrations
text: In church our body prays along with our heart. We stand to praise God and when the Gospel is read, because we stand when someone important is speaking. We bow our heads and sometimes kneel to say sorry and to ask for mercy. A prostration, called a metanoia, is when we kneel and touch the ground with our head or hands, showing humility and worship to God alone. In the Coptic Church we usually do not kneel during the Liturgy on Sundays or during the fifty days after Easter, because those are days of joy. During Lent and the Agpeya we use prostrations more. Follow the deacon, and ask Abouna if you are unsure.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is a deacon?
text: A deacon is a servant of the church. The word deacon means servant. Deacons help the priest during the Holy Liturgy by reading the Bible, singing the hymns, leading the prayers and helping with the altar. In the Coptic Church, boys and men can be ordained as deacons, and there are different ranks. Many children start serving as young deacons and learn the hymns in Coptic and Arabic or English. The first deacons in the Bible were chosen by the apostles to help serve, and one of them was St. Stephen. Deacons wear a white tunic with a colored stole, and they serve with joy and with respect.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What does a priest do?
text: A priest is a servant of God and a shepherd of His people. In the Coptic Church we call him Abouna, which means our father. The priest serves the Holy Liturgy, prays the prayers of the church, baptizes, gives Holy Communion, hears confessions, blesses marriages and visits the sick. He is ordained by a bishop. Priests can be married if they were married before they were ordained, which is common in our church. A priest loves the people of his church like his own family and prays for us each day. When you meet Abouna, you can ask him for a blessing, and you can ask him any question about God and the church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Bishops and the Pope
text: A bishop is the leader of a diocese, which is a group of churches in one region. Bishops are the successors of the apostles, and they ordain priests and deacons, bless the holy oil together and take care of the church. In our church many bishops are monks who gave up the world to live a life of prayer. Above them, the Pope is the head of the whole Coptic Orthodox Church. He is the bishop of Alexandria and the Pope of Alexandria and the Patriarch of the See of St. Mark. He is chosen by the church and ordained as the successor of St. Mark, and we pray for him by name in the Liturgy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who is the Pope of Alexandria?
text: The Pope of Alexandria is the spiritual father and the head of the Coptic Orthodox Church. His full title is the Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the See of St. Mark. He lives in Egypt, where the Church began, and he takes care of Coptic Christians in Egypt and all over the world, including here. He leads the bishops, visits churches and prays for the people. When he visits a church, there is a big celebration, and people sing and ask for his blessing. We remember him in our prayers, and we ask God to keep him safe and wise. You can ask Abouna for the name of the current Pope.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: St. Mark the Apostle, founder of our church
text: St. Mark the Apostle brought the Gospel to Egypt and founded the Church of Alexandria, which is why we are called the Church of St. Mark. He wrote the Gospel of Mark, and tradition tells us that he was one of the seventy apostles, and a helper to St. Peter. The Church teaches that he came to Alexandria, preached about Jesus, and many people believed and were baptized. He became the first Pope of Alexandria, and tradition says he died as a martyr in Alexandria. His story is told in our church tradition, and we honor him as our founder. We thank God for St. Mark and ask for his prayers.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Agpeya and the seven prayers
text: The Agpeya is the Coptic book of the hours. It is our prayer book with the prayers for seven times in the day: Prime in the morning, Terce at the third hour, Sext at the sixth hour, None at the ninth hour, Vespers at sunset, Compline before bed, and the Midnight prayer. The Psalms are the main part of each, with a Gospel reading and short prayers. The book comes from the words of David who said that he praised God seven times a day. A good start for a child is to pray Prime in the morning and Compline before bed. You do not have to pray all seven at once. Start small and grow slowly.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Seven times a day do I praise thee

title: How do we pray?
text: Praying is simply talking and listening to God, like talking to a loving father. You can pray anywhere and at any time. Start by making the sign of the cross, thank God for good things, say sorry for anything you did wrong, and ask Him for help for yourself and others. Then say Amen. You can pray with your own words, with the Lord's Prayer, or with the prayers in the Agpeya. It is good to have a set time each day, like morning, before meals and before bed. You can stand, sit or kneel. God hears every prayer, even a very short one, and He loves to hear from you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is fasting and why do we fast?
text: Fasting means going without some food, or not eating for a period of time, to grow closer to God. It is not a punishment and it is not a diet. We fast to train our body and our heart to say no to what we want and to focus on prayer, so that we can be strong against sin. Fasting also helps us remember the poor and give to them. Fasting always goes together with prayer and doing good. Jesus fasted for forty days in the wilderness. The rules for fasting are different for each person based on age and health, so kids should ask Abouna and their parents what is right for them.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Fasting on Wednesday and Friday
text: In the Coptic Church we fast on most Wednesdays and Fridays during the year. Wednesday is the day when Judas agreed to betray Jesus, and Friday is the day Jesus died on the cross. So these days are for remembering and repenting. We also do not fast on Wednesdays and Fridays during the fifty days after Easter, because that is a time of joy. On a fasting day we abstain from animal products, such as meat, dairy and eggs, and many people eat a vegan style diet, and many fast until the afternoon. The exact rules differ by age and health. Children should ask Abouna and their parents how much to fast.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Great Lent
text: The Great Lent is the long fast before Easter, when we prepare to remember the death and Resurrection of Jesus. It is a time for more prayer, more kindness, more Bible reading and more giving. During Lent we keep a vegan style fast, with no meat or dairy products or eggs, and we eat simple foods. The Great Lent lasts about fifty-five days including Holy Week, and starts with a short fast before it called the Fast of Nineveh. It is not meant to be sad. It is a hopeful time as we walk with Jesus toward Pascha. Children should ask Abouna and parents about what they can fast, since it depends on age and health.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Coptic calendar and Nayrouz
text: The Coptic calendar is the calendar of the Coptic Church, and it comes from ancient Egypt. It has thirteen months, twelve months of thirty days and a little month at the end of five or six days. The new year begins on the first day of the month of Tout, and the feast of that day is called Nayrouz. It usually falls in September in our calendar. Nayrouz means a new year and is a day of joy, but the Church also remembers the martyrs, so the day has a mix of happy and holy feelings. Many of our feasts and saint days are counted by the Coptic calendar. Ask Abouna to show you the date today in Coptic.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Holy Family in Egypt
text: When Jesus was a little child, King Herod wanted to harm Him. An angel told Joseph in a dream to take Mary and Jesus and go to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt and stayed there until it was safe to go home. Because Jesus walked on the land of Egypt, the Coptic Church believes Egypt was blessed. The prophet Isaiah also said that the Lord would come to Egypt, and that there would be an altar to the Lord in the land of Egypt. We remember this journey every year, and we thank God for keeping Jesus safe. Many Egyptians love to visit the places where tradition says the Holy Family stayed.
source: Bible (KJV)

title: Where did the Holy Family stay in Egypt?
text: Church tradition tells us that the Holy Family traveled through many places in Egypt, from the north of the country to the south, and that they were in Egypt for a number of years. Tradition remembers places such as Al-Mataria, Old Cairo, Wadi El Natrun and Al-Muharraq Monastery in Upper Egypt, where tradition says they stayed for a longer time. Many churches in these places honor the visit. Some details come from the tradition of the Church and not from the Bible, so the exact places and the length of time are told in different ways. The Coptic Church celebrates the entrance of the Holy Family into Egypt each year, and we remember it with thanks and joy.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the martyrs?
text: A martyr is a person who loved Jesus so much that they never stopped believing in Him, even when other people were unkind or made things very hard for them. The word martyr means a witness. The first martyr was St. Stephen the deacon. Many Christians in Egypt were martyrs in the early years of the Church, and they stayed faithful to Jesus. We call them heroes of faith, and we believe they are alive with Christ and happy in heaven. We remember them in church and tell their stories, and we ask for their prayers. We can be brave and faithful like them, by being honest and standing up for what is right.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why does the Coptic calendar start from the Era of the Martyrs?
text: The Coptic calendar counts its years from the Era of the Martyrs, which is also called Anno Martyrum. It starts from the year when the Roman emperor Diocletian began his rule, and many Christians in Egypt were martyred during his reign. The Church chose to count the years from then to honor the martyrs and never forget their faith. So the Coptic year number is lower than the regular year number by about 284 years. That means the Coptic year is not the same as the year in the usual calendar. Counting this way is a way to say thank you to all those who held on to Christ through hard times.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What does Coptic mean?
text: The word Coptic comes from an old Greek word for Egypt, and it came to mean the people and the church of Egypt. So the Coptic Church is the church of Egypt, and Copts are the Christians of Egypt. The Coptic language is the last stage of the ancient Egyptian language, written mostly with Greek letters plus a few extra letters. It was spoken in Egypt for many centuries. Today it is used mainly in church for prayers and hymns, and some people in the Church learn to speak it again. In the Liturgy you will hear Coptic, Arabic and English. Some of the words, like Kyrie eleison, come from Greek.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Being ready for Holy Communion
text: Holy Communion is the Body and Blood of Jesus, so we get ready for it with care. We try to confess our sins to our priest, be sorry for what we did wrong, and forgive those who upset us. In the Coptic Church we also fast before Communion, which means we do not eat or drink from the night before until after we receive, and the length depends on age and health. We come to church on time, dress neatly, listen to the Liturgy and pray. Only baptized Orthodox Christians may take Communion. If you are not sure whether you are ready, ask Abouna, and he will help you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Saying sorry and being forgiven
text: Everyone makes mistakes, even grown ups. When we do something wrong, that is called sin. God does not want us to hide or feel afraid. He wants us to tell Him we are sorry and try again. This is called repentance. God is full of love, and He forgives us every time we ask from our heart. In confession, we tell our sins to God with Abouna listening, and Abouna prays that God forgives us. Then we feel light and clean. We should also forgive other people, the way God forgives us. Saying sorry is brave, and it makes us stronger and kinder.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

title: How should we behave in church?
text: The church is the house of God, so we come with joy and respect. We arrive on time, dress neatly, and turn off our phones. We make the sign of the cross when we enter and greet people kindly. During the service we listen, sing and pray, and we do not run, shout or play. We do not talk while the Gospel is read or during the prayers. If we need to leave, we do it quietly. When the Haykal curtain opens, we stay still and look at the altar. After the service we can greet Abouna and our friends. Kind and quiet behavior shows that we love Jesus and care for others.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Bible?
text: The Bible is God's Word, the holy book that tells us about God, His love and His plan to save us. It was written by many people over a long time, but they were inspired by the Holy Spirit. It has two big parts: the Old Testament and the New Testament. The Bible has stories, songs, laws, wise sayings and letters. We read it at home, in Sunday School and in the Liturgy, and the priest explains it. Reading a little each day helps us know God better. The Bible says that God's word is a lamp for our feet and a light for our path.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

title: The Old and New Testaments
text: The Bible has two parts. The Old Testament tells about the time before Jesus came. It has the stories of creation, Adam and Eve, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David and the prophets, and it has the Psalms and the books of wisdom. It points to Jesus who would come. The New Testament tells about the life of Jesus, the four Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, the Acts of the Apostles, the letters of the apostles and the Book of Revelation. The Old and New Testament belong together. The Coptic Church uses the full Old Testament, including the books that some churches leave out, and we read both in church.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the angels?
text: Angels are spiritual beings that God created. They are not people who died, and we do not become angels. Angels worship God, bring His messages and take care of us. In the Bible the angel Gabriel told Mary she would have Jesus, and angels guarded people like Daniel. We know the names of the archangels Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, and we ask them to pray for us. Each person has a guardian angel, according to our Church tradition. We do not worship angels, we only worship God. When you feel scared, you can say a short prayer and remember that angels are near.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.

title: Who are the saints and why do we ask for their prayers?
text: Saints are people who loved God very much and lived holy lives. Now they are alive with Christ in heaven. The Church believes that they still care for us and pray for us. Just like we ask our parents or friends to pray for us, we ask the saints for their prayers. We do not pray to them as gods. We worship only God, and the saints help us by praying with us to Him. The saints include the apostles, the martyrs, the monks and many men and women of faith. We celebrate their feast days, read about their lives, and try to follow their good examples of love, courage and kindness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Cross and Good Friday
text: Good Friday is the day Jesus died on the cross. He did this because He loves us, and He took our sins on Himself so that we could be forgiven and have life with God. It sounds sad, but it is also a day of great love. Jesus did not stay dead. He did this for us all. In the Coptic Church we call the week before Easter Holy Week, and on Good Friday we pray, read the Bible, sing sad hymns, and fast. We make the sign of the cross because the cross shows how much Jesus loves us. The cross is the sign of victory for Christians.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Resurrection
text: On the third day after Jesus died, He rose from the dead. This is the Resurrection, the greatest event in our faith. Early on Sunday morning, the women came to the tomb and found it empty, and an angel told them Jesus had risen. Then Jesus appeared to His disciples and many others, and they were filled with joy. By rising, Jesus defeated death and gave us hope of eternal life. We celebrate this at Easter, which we call the Feast of the Resurrection or Pascha, with a joyful Liturgy at night and a big family meal. We greet each other with Christ is risen, and answer, Truly He is risen.
source: Bible (KJV)

verse.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said.
